title: Standard smooth atlas for a diagonal plane hypersurface
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $n\geq1$, and let $\alpha, eta,\gamma$ be invertible elements of $\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$. Assume that the section $n\cdot1$ is invertible. Let $D\subset\mathbf P^2_S$ be the closed hypersurface $\alpha A^n+ eta B^n+\gamma C^n=0$ [def-pc-proj, def-nagata-projective-space-base-change, def-pc-zero-scheme, def-pc-projective-space-twist]. Its structure morphism $D	o S$ is smooth of relative dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and H-projective [def-kun-projective]. More precisely, over any affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$ each standard projective chart has coordinate ring $Q=R[s,t]/(\lambda s^n+\mu t^n+
u)$, for a permutation $(\lambda,\mu,
u)$ of the restrictions of $(\alpha, eta,\gamma)$. The opens $D(s),D(t)$ cover $\operatorname{Spec}Q$, and their coordinate rings have standard smooth presentations [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra]
$$Q_s\cong R[s,z,t]/(\lambda s^n+\mu t^n+
u,sz-1),\qquad Q_t\cong R[t,z,s]/(\lambda s^n+\mu t^n+
u,tz-1),$$
with Jacobian determinants $\lambda n s^n$ and $\mu n t^n$, respectively, for the first two variables. These presentations and their invertible determinants persist after every ring base change $R	o R'$, and after every map $\operatorname{Spec}L	o S$ with $L$ a field, the resulting opens of $D_L$ have dimension one at each point.

source.place: Tag 0BYA, section-plane-curves, Fermat smoothness calculation; literature/stacks-project/algebra.tex Tag 00T7, lemma-standard-smooth, parts (1), (5), (7); relative unit-coefficient version of returned proof step 4.

proof.text: Write $f:D\to S$ and $F=\alpha A^n+\beta B^n+\gamma C^n$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] with three coordinates. Above an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ the three charts cover projective space, have coordinate rings $R[s,t]$, and the distinguished coordinate trivializes $\mathcal O(1)$. Its $n$th tensor power trivializes $\mathcal O(n)$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. For example on the $C$-chart, $s=A/C$, $t=B/C$, and $F=(\alpha s^n+\beta t^n+\gamma)C^n$. The affine local formula of [lem-pc-zero-scheme-properties](1) therefore identifies $D\cap D_+(C)\cap f^{-1}V$ with $\operatorname{Spec}Q$, where $Q=R[s,t]/(\alpha s^n+\beta t^n+\gamma)$. The $A$- and $B$-charts give the asserted permutations. All coefficients and $n$ remain units under restriction to $V$.

source.place: Tag 0BYA, section-plane-curves, Fermat affine chart calculation; constructions.tex Tag 01NG, lemma-standard-covering-projective-space

proof.text:
Fix one such $Q$ and write $g=\lambda s^n+\mu t^n+
u$. In $Q$ the equation gives $1=-
u^{-1}\lambda s^n-
u^{-1}\mu t^n$. Since $n\geq1$, this is $1=s(-
u^{-1}\lambda s^{n-1})+t(-
u^{-1}\mu t^{n-1})$. A prime of $Q$ cannot contain both $s$ and $t$, so $D(s)\cup D(t)=\operatorname{Spec}Q$. This proof also covers $n=1$ and the zero ring.

source.place: Tag 0BYA, section-plane-curves, unit-ideal argument in the Fermat smoothness calculation, with unit coefficients

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], $D(s)$ and $D(t)$, with their open subscheme structures, are $\operatorname{Spec}Q_s$ and $\operatorname{Spec}Q_t$. Put $B_s=R[s,z,t]/(g,sz-1)$. The map $B_s\to Q_s$ sends $s,t$ to their classes and $z$ to $s^{-1}$. Conversely $Q\to B_s$ sends $s$ to a unit with inverse $z$ and therefore extends uniquely to $Q_s\to B_s$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property]. The composites fix $s,t,z$ and fix every fraction $a/s^r$, respectively, so they are identities. The same construction gives $Q_t\cong R[t,z,s]/(g,tz-1)$, with $z\mapsto t^{-1}$. These are isomorphisms over $R$, so their structural maps are those of the restricted morphism $f$.

In the variable order $(s,z,t)$, the matrix $(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{i,j\leq2}$ for $(f_1,f_2)=(g,sz-1)$ is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\lambda n s^{n-1}&z\\0&s\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Its determinant is $\lambda n s^n$, a unit with inverse $\lambda^{-1}n^{-1}z^n$. In the order $(t,z,s)$ for $(g,tz-1)$ the matrix is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\mu n t^{n-1}&z\\0&t\end{smallmatrix}\right)$; its determinant is $\mu n t^n$ with inverse $\mu^{-1}n^{-1}z^n$. Thus both presentations are standard smooth by [def-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-algebra], with three variables and two relations, hence presentation dimension $3-2=1$.

For every $R	o R'$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-base-change] to the two presentations in step 4. It gives precisely $R'[s,z,t]/(\lambda' s^n+\mu' t^n+
u',sz-1)$ and $R'[t,z,s]/(\lambda' s^n+\mu' t^n+
u',tz-1)$, with the same numbers of variables and relations. The determinants and their inverses are the images of those in step 4. Also $R'\otimes_RQ=R'[s,t]/(\lambda' s^n+\mu' t^n+
u')$: maps out of either algebra are exactly a pair of elements satisfying this equation. Adjoining an inverse to $s$ or $t$ gives the same descriptions of its two localized rings as in step 3. The identity in step 2 maps to the same identity with primed coefficients, so these opens still cover. On schemes these are the actual base-changed charts: the projective-space chart descriptions apply over $R'$, and [lem-pc-zero-scheme-pullback] identifies the pulled-back zero scheme with the zero scheme of the pulled-back section. In particular no flatness of $R	o R'$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 00T7, lemma-standard-smooth (5) and its coefficientwise proof; local coefficient description of the zero scheme under pullback

proof.text: The two algebras of step 4 are smooth over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-is-smooth]. Their spectra are smooth over $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine]. Their identifications with the open subschemes of $D$ are over $V$, so smoothness transfers along them by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes](c); part (b) of that node then makes each of these open subschemes smooth over $S$. Varying $V$ and the three projective charts gives a cover of $D$ by step 1, refined by the two opens of step 2. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source] to this cover to conclude that $f:D\to S$ is smooth. This includes an empty base or empty chart, for which the covering criterion is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 01V6, lemma-smooth-characterize (1)-(3); algebra.tex Tag 00T7 (1); open-target composition as in Tags 01VC and 01VA

proof.text: Let $h:\operatorname{Spec}L\to S$ with $L$ a field. $\operatorname{Spec}L$ has one point [def-weil-affine-spectrum], so choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ containing its image; $h$ factors through $V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. Step 5 applied to $R\to L$ gives a covering of $D_L$ by standard smooth affine schemes with three variables and two relations. By [lem-weil-pbc-standard-smooth-over-field-dimension-at-points] each such open has dimension $3-2=1$ at every one of its points. This is dimension at a point in [def-kun-dimension], not the dimension of a local ring. If $x\in U\subset X$ with $U$ open, every open neighbourhood $W$ of $x$ contains $W\cap U$. A strict chain of nonempty irreducible closed subsets in $W\cap U$ gives such a chain of the same length in $W$ by taking closures: intersecting those closures with $W\cap U$ recovers the original subsets, so strictness is preserved. Thus $\dim(W\cap U)\leq\dim W$, which is also [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone] with $U'=W\cap U\subseteq W$. The open neighbourhoods of $x$ in $U$ are also open in $X$, and the two minima in the definition are therefore equal: $\dim_x U=\dim_x X$ directly from that definition. Hence $\dim_x D_L=1$ for every $x\in D_L$. Taking $L=\kappa(s)$ for every $s\in S$, together with step 6, is exactly smoothness of relative dimension one in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

Finally the given closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^2_S$, followed by the structural projection, is $f$. Taking $N=2$ in [def-kun-projective] proves that $f$ is H-projective; no properness or ampleness criterion is required.
